### User Interface Modeling Workflow 1. Read the existing User Interface model to understand current Pages, Components, and Diagrams. 2. Discover candidate Service Operations (Commands, Queries, or other Service Operations) exposed over HTTP. Search across ALL applications in the solution, not just the current one — a qualifying operation may live in a different application than the User Interface package. 3. Selecting among candidates: - If exactly one operation clearly satisfies the requirement, use it without asking. - If multiple operations could plausibly satisfy the requirement, ASK the user which to use. - If NO operation satisfies the requirement, STOP and ask the user whether to create one, use a different one, or confirm no backend call is needed. Do not create the page until this is resolved. 4. If the chosen operation lives in a Service Package not yet referenced by the User Interface package, add that package reference before continuing. 5. Design and create the Pages and Components needed to meet the requirement, placing each into a logically-named folder rather than directly under the root "Pages" folder (see folder rule below). 6. For each new routable Page (or a Page Operation on it), add a `Call Service Operation Action` to the operation selected in step 3, and place it on the diagram. A Page must not exist without either this action modeled or explicit user confirmation that no backend call is needed. 7. Add `Navigation` associations between Pages wherever a button, link, or other UI element gives the user an explicit way to move from one Page to another. 8. Add `Show Dialog` associations wherever a Page or Component explicitly triggers a dialog. 9. Add `Composition` associations connecting Components to the Pages, dialogs, and other Components that contain them. 10. Lay out all Pages, Navigations, dialogs, and Service Operation calls on the diagram (creating the diagram first if it doesn't exist). 11. If asked to add, model or similar a page, dialog, component, etc, you MUST model it in the UI designer. You should NEVER only code it directly, unless explicitly asked to.
### User Interface Modeling Rules
- Model backend interactions ONLY via `Call Service Operation Action`, called directly from a Page or Component. Never create, rename, delete, or otherwise use Component Operations for this. - A Service Operation must be exposed over HTTP if it lives in an application other than the current User Interface's application. [If there's a specific tool/attribute that confirms HTTP exposure, name it here.] - A bidirectional Navigation between two Pages must be modeled as a single bidirectional association — never as two separate one-directional associations. - Do not add new Pages, Components, or dialogs directly under the root "Pages" folder. Group them into logically-named subfolders (e.g. by feature area, workflow, or domain concept) that reflect how they relate to one another. Only place an element at the root if it genuinely doesn't belong to any grouping — this should be the exception, not the default.
### User Interface Diagram Rules
- Space Pages apart, grouping them by conceptual relationship and by how many Navigations connect them, so associations don't overlap. - Place Service Operations to the right of the Pages that call them, stacked vertically with 100px between each, and at least [Npx] of horizontal space from the Pages column. - Route Navigation and Show Dialog associations so they don't overlap Page or Service Operation boxes.
